column3: Close to the Hebrew.
“That the leaders led” renders a difficult phrase, often read “when locks hung loose” or “when leaders took the lead”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“the field of Edom” renders “the region of Edom.”
“quaked” renders a verb that may mean “flowed” or “quaked”; the meaning is uncertain.
“were deserted” renders “ceased”; “roundabout ways” renders “twisting roads.”
“The peasantry” renders a rare word, also read “village life” or “warriors”; the meaning is uncertain.
“war was in the gates” renders a difficult phrase, read by some as “bread of the gates”; the meaning is uncertain.
“goes out to” renders “is for.”
“white donkeys” renders “tawny female donkeys”; “rich carpets” renders “cloths,” and “sing” renders “tell out.”
“those who divide flocks” renders a rare word, also read “archers” or “singers”; “peasantry” is uncertain as in verse 7.
“take away your captives” renders “take captive your captives.”
The Hebrew of this verse is difficult; NASB’s “survivors came down to the nobles” is one reading.
“those who wield the staff of office” renders “those who march with the staff of a muster officer”; the meaning of the first line is uncertain.
“the princes of Issachar” renders “my princes in Issachar”; “rushed at his heels” renders “was sent at his feet.”
“sheepfolds” renders a rare word for hearths or saddlebags; “piping for the flocks” renders “whistling of the flocks.”
“stay in ships” renders “sojourn ships”; the meaning is uncertain.
“despised their lives even to death” renders “despised its life to die.”
“plunder in silver” renders “profit of silver.”
“courses” renders “highways.”
“The torrent” renders “the wadi”; “O my soul, march on with strength” renders a terse line whose meaning is uncertain.
“valiant steeds” renders “mighty ones.”
“Utterly curse” renders the doubled verb; “warriors” renders “mighty ones.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “him”; “a magnificent bowl” renders “a bowl of nobles.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“dead” renders “destroyed.”
“lamented” renders a rare verb; “tarry” renders “delay.”
“would answer” renders “answered.”
“A maiden, two maidens” renders the crude “a womb, two wombs”; “every warrior” renders “the head of a man,” and “the spoiler” renders “the plunder.”
